pages.abox.hero.title: Portable Boombox A-BOX
pages.abox.story.0.title: Rugged Audio Box
pages.abox.story.0.text.0: A-BOX started as a simple idea: build a portable speaker that felt more like a small piece of equipment than a fragile consumer device inspired by dutch brand Thodio .
pages.abox.story.0.text.1: From component sourcing to enclosure work, the project was an opportunity to practice building something from the ground up, with a focus on making it feel solid and durable in hand.
pages.abox.story.1.title: Electronics
pages.abox.story.1.text.0: Internal wiring, power management decisions and a small custom PCB to keep the final assembly cleaner.
pages.abox.story.1.text.1: It was an early but valuable exercise in making electronics physically robust, not just functional on a table.
pages.abox.story.2.title: Final Assembly
pages.abox.story.2.text.0: The final work was as much about finish and usability as electronics: making the enclosure look intentional, protect the internals and remain convenient to carry and operate.
pages.aquilo.hero.title: AQUILO Student Rocket Team
pages.aquilo.disclosure.label: Disclosure
pages.aquilo.disclosure.text: Knowledge Embargo: I will only disclose non-sensitive information regarding my work at AQUILO.
pages.aquilo.story.0.title: Action = Reaction
pages.aquilo.story.0.text.0: As a part of the propulsion department of AQUILO Student Rocket Team, I have been involved in the design, manufacturing, and testing of solid rocket motors.
pages.aquilo.story.0.text.1: AQUILO, a passionate team, dedicated to passing down rocketry knowledge and pushing the limits of student innovation has been my stepping mile into field of aerospace engineering enhancing my knowledge regarding propulsion and component design.
pages.aquilo.story.0.text.2: Check out AQUILO VIII.S launch slow-mo!
pages.aquilo.story.1.title: Everyday Work
pages.aquilo.story.1.text.0: Responsible engineer of HEI Head-End Ignition project. Project gave me the oportunity to delve deep into propulsion concepts in rocket engineering. My project advances the teams capabilities in terms of ignition of dual stage rocket designs with current motor achitecture. HEI boosts grain ignition time which as a result brings higher overall propulsion ISP (specific impulse).
pages.aquilo.story.1.text.1: HEI boosts grain ignition time which as a result brings higher overall propulsion ISP (specific impulse).
pages.aquilo.story.2.title: From design to flight
pages.aquilo.story.2.text.0: I have used my machining skills to produce various components for our rocket motors. From endcaps to nozzles, I have been involved in the manufacturing process of critical parts of our propulsion system. This has given me a hands-on experience with various manufacturing techniques and materials used in aerospace engineering. But things do not stop at propulsion, I have also been involved in manufacturing and advising on other structural components of VIII.S rocket. From body struts to retaining rings, I have enjoyed the process of turning a design into a physical part fullfilling its purpose.
pages.aquilo.story.2.text.1: But things do not stop at propulsion, I have also been involved in manufacturing and advising on other structural components of VIII.S rocket. From body struts to retaining rings, I have enjoyed the process of turning a design into a physical part fullfilling its purpose.

My role involves maintaining and operating flight simulators, ensuring their optimal performance for pilot training at specific certification level.
pages.cae.story.1.text.1: Want to see more about my internship work at CAE?

pages.cavitation.hero.title: Orifice Cavitation Analysis
pages.cavitation.facts.title: At a glance
pages.cavitation.facts.deliverables.v: Interactive test database, data processing pipeline, research outcome
pages.cavitation.note.label: Disclosure
pages.cavitation.note.text: This page only uses non-proprietary information. Specific operating conditions, hardware details and performance data are intentionally excluded.
pages.cavitation.thesis.title: Research
pages.cavitation.thesis.text: This project formed my Bachelor thesis and focused on cavitation onset in orifice restriction plates of HELIX engine, with primary focus being fuel and ignition feed lines.
pages.cavitation.thesis.point.0: Empirical comparison of different cavitation onset effects
pages.cavitation.thesis.point.1: Structured data processing for repeatable test comparison
pages.cavitation.story.why.title: Why Cavitation Matters
pages.cavitation.story.why.text.0: Flow can behave very differently once cavitation starts. For propulsion systems, predicting that onset is important because it affects stability, component sizing and test interpretation.
pages.cavitation.story.why.text.1: The work focused on building a practical understanding of cavitation behavior of engine specific components and magnitude of testing deviations.
pages.cavitation.pid.title: Simplified P&ID
pages.cavitation.pid.text: The diagram shows the structure of the investigation only at a high level. The test rig could control upstream flow conditions while collecting data from independent measurement points along the path, providing a precise flow characterization.
pages.cavitation.pid.article.v: Set of restriction plates with varying geometries.
pages.cavitation.story.flow.title: Flow characteristics
pages.cavitation.story.flow.text.0: Research on cavitation often focuses on detailed system-specific behavior. Goal was to find a way how to determine the threshold of cavitation onset to minimize test descrepancies and enable repeatable comparison of different test runs and their flow characteristics.
pages.cavitation.story.analysis.title: Analysis Workflow
pages.cavitation.story.analysis.text.0: The dataset from the test rig was processed where onset trends were compared across different test runs and hardware configurations.
pages.cavitation.story.analysis.text.1: Final deliverables included an interactive TOML database of test results and a structured data processing pipeline using Python to enable repeatable analysis of future tests.
pages.cavitation.story.analysis.text.2: The results match theoretical behavior of flow as can be seen from previous sketch.
pages.cnce.hero.title: CNC Engraver
pages.cnce.facts.title: At a glance
pages.cnce.note.label: Archive note
pages.cnce.note.text: This is an older project, but it captures the early hands-on route into CNC, electronics and motion control.
pages.cnce.story.0.title: Improvised Motion
pages.cnce.story.0.text.0: The engraver was built from salvaged optical-drive mechanics, which made it a compact way to learn how stepper motion, guides, backlash and frame stiffness interact.
pages.cnce.story.0.text.1: It was not about creating a production machine. It was about making a limited set of parts move predictably enough to engrave and learning from every compromise.
pages.cnce.story.1.title: Control
pages.cnce.story.1.text.0: The controller side introduced me to GRBL-style motion control, wiring discipline and the practical side of building CNC systems.
pages.cnce.story.1.text.1: As an early project, it became a useful foundation for later CNC and machining work.
pages.cncl.hero.title: CNC Lathe Retrofit
pages.cncl.facts.title: At a glance
pages.cncl.facts.deliverables.v: Working CAM pipeline and machined validation parts
pages.cncl.note.label: Project scope
pages.cncl.note.text: The page focuses on the retrofit process and visible outcomes. Machine-specific configuration details are kept concise so the page stays useful without becoming a service manual.
pages.cncl.story.0.title: Idea
pages.cncl.story.0.text.0: The retrofit started during the design phase of the HEI project, where manufacturing access and machining capability had a direct influence on possible design decisions.
pages.cncl.story.0.text.1: The school-owned CNC lathe had been unused for a long period, but the machine still had valuable capability. The goal was to make it approachable again through a modern CAM workflow.
pages.cncl.story.1.title: Troubleshooting
pages.cncl.story.1.text.0: Before touching the software workflow, the machine needed basic recovery work: lubrication, checks of subcomponents, controller exploration and calibration.
pages.cncl.story.1.text.1: With the SINUMERIK 810D controller operational, the next challenge was making Fusion CAM output code that the machine could read reliably.
pages.cncl.story.2.title: CAM Workflow
pages.cncl.story.2.text.0: The available post-processor was close, but not compatible enough with the controller version running on the machine. After iterative testing and manufacturer communication, I tuned the post-processor so the generated CAM code was usable on the lathe.
pages.cncl.story.2.text.1: The final result was a clearer path from CAD to CAM to machine, making the equipment more useful for student projects.

pages.extras.hero.title: Extras
pages.extras.hero.summary: A small glimpse at the things that keep me curious when I step away from CAD, theory and hardware.
pages.extras.intro.title: Motion, places and quiet resets.
pages.extras.intro.text.0: Outside of engineering, I am drawn to activities that mix attention, movement and a bit of controlled chaos: FPV flying, riding, snowboarding, travel and photography.
pages.extras.intro.text.1: They are different from engineering work, but they support the same habit: noticing details, learning by doing and staying comfortable when things are not perfectly predictable.
pages.extras.moments.title: A Few Things I Come Back To
pages.extras.moments.0.title: Snowboarding
pages.extras.moments.0.text: As a professional snowboard instructor, snowboarding is one of the cleanest ways I know to reset: freedom, fast feedback and simple rules.
pages.extras.moments.1.title: Motorbike
pages.extras.moments.1.text: Good roads, good weather and a airflow passing over the face. Right balance means everything.
pages.extras.moments.2.title: Firesport
pages.extras.moments.2.text: This competitive sport combines team spirit and individual performance.
pages.extras.moments.3.title: Places that make me look up
pages.extras.moments.3.text: Travel and aerospace history keep the larger picture close: engineering is still about wonder.
pages.extras.closing.text: Not everything has to become a project. Some things are just there to keep the mind sharp, the body moving and the week a little more alive.
pages.gsx.hero.title: GSX-1 Wireframe Sculpture
pages.gsx.facts.title: At a glance
pages.gsx.facts.focus.v: Compact sensor interface and clean physical layout
pages.gsx.story.0.title: Inspiration
pages.gsx.story.0.text.0: GSX-1 started as a small wireframe sculpture inspired by electronics-as-art builds, where the circuit and the structure are part of the same visual language as the one build by Mohit Bhoite.
pages.gsx.story.0.text.1: The challenge was to keep the wiring tidy enough to feel intentional while still fitting the microcontroller, GPS-related module, sensors and display element into a very small footprint.
pages.gsx.story.1.title: Electronics
pages.gsx.story.1.text.0: I built the wiring scheme around an RP2040-based controller and wrote the control logic in C++ through the Arduino toolchain.
pages.gsx.story.1.text.1: The focus was not only making it work, but also making the signal routing and physical assembly tidy when viewed up close.
pages.gsx.story.2.title: Interface
pages.gsx.story.2.text.0: The visible software layer is intentionally minimal: a small interface, clean startup behavior and enough feedback to make the object feel alive without turning it into a gadget demo.
pages.gsx.story.2.text.1: This made the project a useful exercise in balancing technical density with visual restraint.

pages.hei.hero.title: Head-End Ignition
pages.hei.facts.title: At a glance
pages.hei.facts.deliverables.v: Prototype hardware, production components, design report
pages.hei.note.label: Disclosure
pages.hei.note.text: Knowledge embargo: this page only includes non-sensitive information. Propellant-specific details, performance data and proprietary design information are intentionally omitted.
pages.hei.story.idea.title: Idea
pages.hei.story.idea.text.0: Solid rocket motors are reliable and straightforward thrust sources, but characterizing propellants is difficult because small composition changes can strongly affect combustion.
pages.hei.story.idea.text.1: The project explored the idea of a hardware solution that can expand the team capability while avoiding repeated redesigns of the full motor endcap for each test iteration.
pages.hei.story.constraints.title: Design Constraints
pages.hei.story.constraints.text: Since upgrade required redesign of the motor endcap, this oportunity was used to implement a head-end ignition system that could be reused across multi-rocket configurations. After exploring options, the well-tested head-end ignition concept by Richard Nakka as a reference point, then adapted the concept around the team's motor architecture.
pages.hei.story.constraints.bullet.0: Material selection: availability, mass and ESD properties
pages.hei.story.constraints.bullet.1: Retention method: compatibility with current motor hardware
pages.hei.story.constraints.bullet.2: Size constraints: limited circumference and assembly access
pages.hei.story.constraints.bullet.3: Operational envelope: designed around non-disclosed pressure and thermal constraints
pages.hei.story.prototype.title: Prototype
pages.hei.story.prototype.text.0: A first prototype helped verify whether the chosen geometry could be produced with the available machinery and whether the assembly process was realistic at the scale required.
pages.hei.story.prototype.text.1: This early manufacturing pass was especially useful because the design needed to stay practical, not just theoretically elegant.
pages.hei.story.production.title: Final Production
pages.hei.story.production.text.0: With support from Microlan Aerospace, the project moved from prototype parts to a small set of production components for campaign use.
pages.hei.story.production.text.1: Testing and further development were handed over to the current AQUILO propulsion team, keeping the project alive beyond the initial design and manufacturing phase.

pages.machining.story.0.title: Manufacturing Practice
pages.machining.story.0.text.0: Machining became an important part of my engineering workflow because it connects design decisions directly to material, setup time, tool access and inspection.
pages.machining.story.0.text.1: Working on student-team hardware gave me repeated exposure to parts that had to be practical, robust and manufacturable with the machines available.
pages.machining.story.1.title: Propulsion Components
pages.machining.story.1.text.0: Endcaps, nozzles and retention hardware require careful attention to geometry, surface finish, material selection and repeatability.
pages.machining.story.1.text.1: The work helped me understand how design details that look minor in CAD can become important during setup, fixturing or inspection.
pages.machining.story.2.title: Structural Work
pages.machining.story.2.text.0: Beyond propulsion hardware, I also worked on structural pieces and supporting fixtures where repeatability and a clear manufacturing sequence mattered more than complexity for its own sake.
pages.machining.story.2.text.1: Later, I have become advisor for members of the team planning on manufacturing components, helping them understand the tradeoffs and practicalities of different approaches.

pages.rfa.hero.title: Rocket Factory Augsburg AG
pages.rfa.disclosure.label: Disclosure
pages.rfa.disclosure.text: Non-Disclosure Agreement: I only share non-proprietary information regarding my work at RFA. Images and media shown here are publicly available.
pages.rfa.story.0.title: Building Rockets Like Cars
pages.rfa.story.0.text.0: Rocket Factory Augsburg AG is one of the first commercial European companies developing orbital class launcher capable of delivering variety of payloads to different orbits.
pages.rfa.story.0.text.1: Its uniqueness stands in successful full in-house development of Europe's first oxygen-rich staged combustion (ORSC) engine called HELIX capable of delivering roughly 100kN of thrust.
pages.rfa.story.1.title: My Work
pages.rfa.story.1.text.0: As part of the propulsion R&D team, I contributed to development of HELIX, specifically cavitation influence research on component testing.
pages.rfa.story.1.text.1: Key projects I have been involved in include:
pages.rfa.story.1.bullet.1: Cavitation research of propellant/ignition feed system
pages.rfa.story.1.bullet.2: Development of test rigs for component testing
pages.rfa.story.2.title: From design to real production
pages.rfa.story.2.text.0: Involved in the complete development cycle, from defining requirements and design, through validation testing, to final assembly.
pages.rfa.story.2.text.1: Even as an intern, I had the opportunity to see my work implemented in real production. The company’s culture is built on trust — interns are given full responsibility for their projects, supported by strong technical supervision.
pages.sound.hero.title: Sound Analysis
pages.sound.facts.title: At a glance
pages.sound.facts.role.v: Measurement setup, troubleshooting and data interpretation
pages.sound.facts.focus.v: Finding causes of out-of-tolerance sound values
pages.sound.note.label: Disclosure
pages.sound.note.text: This page describes the measurement approach at portfolio level. Simulator-specific certification data and internal operational details are not disclosed.
pages.sound.story.0.title: Problem
pages.sound.story.0.text.0: During certification-related work, sound measurements can fall outside expected tolerance with respect to the aircraft test flight data. The challenge was to understand whether the issue came from setup, acquisition, environment or simulator-specific behavior.
pages.sound.story.0.text.1: The work required a structured approach because audio issues can be deceptively difficult: small changes in placement, routing or configuration can change the result.
pages.sound.story.1.title: Measurement Workflow
pages.sound.story.1.text.0: I worked through the acquisition chain, comparing measurement conditions, microphone placement and repeatability across multiple simulator platforms including statistical analysis of the data to identify patterns and potential causes.
pages.sound.story.1.text.1: The main goal was narrowing the search space and building a clearer troubleshooting sequence for future sound measurement issues.
pages.sound.story.2.title: Implementation of Changes
pages.sound.story.2.text.0: After troubleshooting and listing potential causes, I implemented changes to the measurement setup and acquisition process on system level.
pages.sound.story.2.text.1: The deviations were majorly minimized after the changes, and the work provided a clearer path for future sound measurement troubleshooting.

pages.tail.hero.title: Tail Structural Design
pages.tail.facts.title: At a glance
pages.tail.facts.focus.v: Weight, stiffness, manufacturability and load transfer
pages.tail.story.0.title: Design Intent
pages.tail.story.0.text.0: The tail structure was developed around a set of design requirements where stiffness, load path clarity and manufacturability had to be balanced within a compact assembly.
pages.tail.story.0.text.1: The useful part of the project was not only reaching a final geometry, but justifying why the chosen concept made sense under the given constraints.
pages.tail.story.1.title: Engineering Tradeoffs
pages.tail.story.1.text.0: We looked at how the structure would transfer loads, where material was actually needed and which details would create unnecessary manufacturing difficulty.
pages.tail.story.1.text.1: That made the project a good exercise in defending design decisions rather than simply making the model look finished.
pages.tail.story.2.title: To Actual Flight
pages.tail.story.2.text.0: Close collaboration with the team was key to making the project come together.
pages.tail.story.2.text.1: Our tail section has been the lightest design of the class and took large amount of succesful flights including being selected as a tail section for maiden flight of the overall aircraft.
